title: Scoped public command execution
description: The public command contract consumed by a user or skill-guided participant: explicit requests yield actual bounded observations and side-effect outcomes without conferring engineering decisions.

operations.name: execute_public_request
operations.purpose: Execute one admitted public command within its declared command-family scope.
inputs: Supported command family, version domain, explicit selectors and actor-supplied arguments or request.
Applicable project context and authority for any requested side effect.
outputs: The command family's declared human or structured result, exit outcome, diagnostics, omitted-detail access where applicable, and accurate mutation or no-mutation disposition.

For target operational families, MOD-010 defines the exact closed JSON envelope, primary diagnostic codes, null/omission rules and status/commit/exit mapping. A saved storage outcome is not approval or lifecycle progression.
behavior: Reject unknown commands, unsupported versions, malformed selectors, and invalid modes under the family-specific early-error contract.
Dispatch supported operational tasks through IF-003 and installation through IF-006. Browser IF-012 remains designed separately and is not advertised as implemented by this executable.
Keep recorded values separate from observations and bounded advice. Preserve conflict, unchanged, failed, partial, and committed outcomes rather than converting them to workflow judgments.
Protect private diagnostic content and provide the supported route to materially omitted detail; output bounds cannot hide failures or make a valid correction unrecordable.
Permit standalone skills to avoid command use; governed recording uses an explicit supported request, not implicit installation or inferred state changes.

Honor each family's help/version and invalid-input ordering before repository or stdin access where required, including independent early-error response versions. Omit unavailable identities instead of inventing a validated stored contract.
Capabilities reports actual task/contract availability and observed backend standing; Change context requires explicit scope. Do not discover or select workflow authority from directory residue.

Preserve selected content, optional absence and deliberate omissions with a bounded complete selector index. Serialize the complete bounded result before emission; no cursor or diagnostic-continuation protocol is implied and narrative must not be silently truncated.

For v2/v4 mutations, normalize the selected task into the typed IF-003 request. MOD-011 owns fresh candidate construction, dependency validation and the database transaction. Before commit, establish bounded receipt readiness using the shared MOD-010-owned pure encoder and the selected fixed receipt profile. No SQL, connection, filesystem reader or arbitrary construction/render callback is a v4 request value.

Preview makes no engineering-record or attachment-publication changes and reserves nothing; temporary admission leases and SQLite-internal recovery follow the v4 storage contract. V4 ordinary transactions are recovered internally by SQLite; interrupted store replacement uses explicit maintenance resume. Browser recovery remains separately scoped. No retry implicitly replays old intent or renews a decision basis.

Keep private invocation diagnostics bounded and independent of semantic results, stdout, authoritative repository bytes, and transaction/recovery behavior. Validate closed logging options at the declared admission boundary, protect owned paths and sensitive input, and expose exact-ID lookup as read-only diagnosis rather than command replay or workflow evidence.

For SR074–077 maintenance, preserve the owning MOD011 contract: transfer composes backup and same-project absent-destination restoration; migration requires source stability, preserved originals and explicit current-consumer disposition. No new public operation or automatic authority is inferred from this composition.

failure_behavior.condition: The requested operation is unknown, unsupported, malformed, or outside its admitted scope.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return the applicable family-specific error without downstream side effects; do not guess a corrected request.

failure_behavior.condition: The selected operation reports conflict, incomplete effects, failed access, or required recovery.
failure_behavior.outcome: Preserve that actual result and its safe next decision boundary without asserting successful progression or silently repeating a mutation.

operations.name: query_subject_history
operations.purpose: Admit and present the separately proposed bounded subject-history lookup.
inputs: Explicit associated project, finite retained Change scope, recorded subject key or exact original basis, literal supported filters, page bound and optional state-bound continuation.
preconditions: The separately proposed history profile and complete cooperating writer/maintenance population are qualified; current v2/v4 support does not imply this capability.
outputs: Bounded complete result units with originating Change/record/subject identities, normalized selection, captured history state, coverage limits, exhaustion and optional continuation; or explicit invalid, conflict, busy, unavailable or too-large outcome.
behavior: Apply MOD-011 history-selection.md: MOD-010 owns admission/public presentation; MOD-011 owns recorded associations, coherent read snapshot, ordering and authenticated continuation.
Preserve original facts and partial/unavailable scope; no semantic relevance, current approval inference, implicit history reconstruction or mutation.
Keep the separate proposed operation distinct from current ordinary query grammar, schema and no-cursor result semantics.

MOD-010 performs structural and independently known request checks only; MOD-011 authenticates the opaque continuation and checks bound selection and captured state before any page results, retaining its key and state authority.

failure_behavior.condition: Association/retention coverage is missing, source/profile is unavailable, or selected scope is unreadable.
failure_behavior.outcome: Expose the actual missing or incomplete scope; do not present an empty complete history or initialize, recover or migrate storage.

failure_behavior.condition: Continuation identity/state/selection fails or bounded complete output cannot be formed.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return the specified bounded rejection without silent restart, partial conflicting page, omitted narrative or cursor advance past an unreturned unit.

consistency_rules: The command result must reflect actual effects. A completed write cannot be reported as an unperformed plan or a rejected operation because optional reporting was incomplete.
Scope and authority remain attributable to the supplied request; a skill, role label, or successful command is not a new authorization.
Human and machine-facing outcomes retain the owning command family's distinctions and exit behavior.

Public result domains remain independent of stored records and of installation and diagnostic interfaces. In particular, unsupported or unavailable stored content cannot justify a fabricated validated revision or a guessed response version.
compatibility_rules: The supported CLI Design owns current executable contracts. MOD-010 owns the proposed targeted-recording-v2 and store-maintenance-v1 syntax and result shapes; this Interface defines their responsibility boundary without introducing another RPC or network protocol.
Skill-guided consumers must use supported command contracts and cannot assume new REM model operations exist.
Public contract changes must reconcile all invoking skill guidance, examples, and affected consumers before adoption.

The proposed browser-v1 request/result family is defined by MOD-010 and IF-012; it is not a v2 operational-record command or an observed public entry. Existing command/record behavior remains version-scoped until coordinated adoption.

Skills use supported public tasks, task schemas and opaque revision expectations. They do not need SQL, database schema versions, tables or runtime coordination paths; backend realization is owned by MOD-011. Target tasks cannot be advertised as installed before implementation and qualified adoption.

The deliberately installed successor executable implements v2/v4 operational commands only. Retained v3 operation clauses describe the preceding package, not a parallel dispatcher. Help/read semantics follow executing package identity; unknown/legacy input and absent v4 storage never trigger backend fallback. Explicit qualified import remains the sole successor legacy-data entrypoint.

The proposed subject-history operation is separately qualified under MOD-011 history-selection.md. Existing targeted-recording-v2/current v4 requests and installed command availability remain unchanged; no implicit cursor or association migration is introduced.

sources.basis: Connect common guided invocation to the public command responsibility without weakening CLI ownership or making every skill depend on CLI; see SRC-PUBLISHED-CLI and SRC-PUBLISHED-SKILLS.

Reconcile IR-008 acceptance outcomes and its allocated obligations with explicit command/persistence cooperation, preserving existing CLI/Record Format authority and external-edit limits. The refinement supplies no new executable or public wire format.

Apply refined REM Architecture Design through subordinate observed and proposed views. Preserve the logical allocation, existing public contracts, and draft status; source mapping is not executed satisfaction evidence.

The existing public command contract and local process binding serve external users and agents. Expose the same contract through Engineering operations; MOD-010 remains the sole provider and MOD-012 remains its declared Module consumer.

Refine contract accountability: MOD-018 provides IF-004 and MOD-019 provides IF-006. MOD-010 and MOD-014 retain their behavioral allocations and state responsibilities. This supersedes the provider/exposure choice recorded by SRC-MODULE-HIERARCHY without changing Interface guarantees, consumers, Function/AR allocations, or realization observations. Earlier source entries retain their prior design meaning; this draft refinement supplies no runtime adoption or satisfaction evidence.

System and Architecture Design from SR-084–088 and refined SR-060; proposed responsibility, contract and realization only. No implementation, platform qualification or product availability is established.
Refine existing maintenance cooperation, same-project transfer, preserved-source migration and resumption boundaries without new requirements, public operations or runtime qualification.

Define recorded subject association, coherent bounded history selection and state-bound continuation through existing command/storage owners. Target Design only; current ordinary queries, schema and installed capability remain unchanged.
